What is fine-tuning in machine learning?

Fine-tuning takes a model that was already pretrained on lots of data and continues training it on a smaller, specific dataset. This adapts the model to a particular task, domain, or style without having to train from scratch.

LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) freezes the original model weights and trains a small set of extra 'adapter' matrices instead. Because these adapters are tiny compared to the full model, training is much faster and uses far less memory, while still letting the model learn new behavior.

Give me one tip for writing good training data.
Make your examples look exactly like the real inputs and outputs you want at inference time. Consistency in format and tone matters more than sheer quantity.
How many examples do I need to fine-tune?
You can see useful behavior changes with as few as 50–100 high-quality examples, but a few hundred to a few thousand gives more reliable results. Quality and consistency beat quantity.
